Cover Letter

Hi Netflix,

For 9+ years I’ve been the person who shows up when an office doesn’t exist yet and leaves once it runs itself — playbooks written, vendors, budgets in line, and a system in place so the next office doesn’t have to start from zero. I contributed to 175+ projects across 278,000+ sqm for a 50,000+ person organisation spanning CIS, EU, APAC, and the Americas, and I led the largest project in our Polish portfolio while in Georgia — proof that a good operating model travels better than I do.

Confession: I've been watching Netflix, obsessively, since university. My watch history has zero genre consistency — Stranger Things one night, Emily in Paris and Bridgerton the next, Squid Game and The Diplomat somewhere in between. Turns out that’s basically how I approach projects too: no template, just whatever the story needs — industrial heritage in Belgrade, a brand built from scratch in Tbilisi, an 8,000 sqm HQ in Poland nobody had attempted locally.

The role description — owning the global Workplace program portfolio, the vendor rhythm, the metrics leadership relies on — maps closely to what I already do day to day.

I’d welcome the chance to bring that experience to Netflix. More detail below.

Episode 01 · Building systems, not just spaces
We didn’t have a playbook.
So we started writing one.
EPAM Systems · 50,000+ Employees · Global
When I joined, there were no standards, no metrics, no shared framework for how offices should look or feel. Just a company operating across 50+ countries — and the question of how to make the experience consistent from India to Latin America.

I was part of building it from the ground up: contributing to design guidelines, gathering analytics on what people actually use and love, documenting what worked and what didn’t so new locations wouldn’t repeat the same mistakes, turning that into dos & don’ts for vendors, and pulling in colleagues both inside and outside the company along the way. Everything grounded in real projects, refined across markets.

What actually got built: operational guidelines, SLAs, and vendor onboarding structures to govern how work gets done; measurement standards and ratios to keep decisions grounded in data; brandbooks and documented best practices to keep design consistent across markets; and the collaboration layer around it — cross-department workflows, stakeholder approval flow, onboarding sessions for new locations, and employee satisfaction analysis to track what was actually working.

Today: a growing system with real data behind it — metrics, patterns, and a library of use cases that informs every new office we open.
Episode 02 · Krakow, Poland
Reinventing how a HQ works
European HQ · 8,000 m²
Kitchen hubs as the social heart of each floor for people to actually gather, not just grab coffee. We also built large event zones hosting everything from yoga to full conferences, plus a self-contained client lounge built like an airport business lounge.

The real achievement was stakeholder buy-in: convincing a team used to solo-work patterns and private offices to embrace shared, activity-based space instead — and the project became the reference other locations now look to.
Episode 03 · Belgrade, Serbia
Brand meets heritage
BIGZ Building · State Printing House, 1937 · 2,690 m²
The biggest challenge here wasn’t just protecting the historical architecture, but introducing the company’s brand and character into it.

What makes this project stand out: the developer pushed through and built the bold architectural forms in the design as planned, despite building legalisation issues, budget pressure, and a change in the developer’s own management along the way. The project was delivered.
Episode 04 · Tbilisi, Georgia
Finding the brand from scratch
New physical identity · 2024
The brand had just changed and only existed in digital form — nobody knew yet what it should look like in physical space. Construction had already started, so there was no time to wait for a new brandbook. We designed and experimented as we went: wave ceiling, iridescent panels, chromatic palette.
